text:
Alex: Quick update — spike work for FP8 enablement on H100/L40S for gpt-medium. After running calibration + kernel selection we get ~8-12% median throughput win but seeing accuracy drift on a few prompts and occasional NaNs in attention kernels. Anyone seen this pattern?

Maya: can you paste the profiler + transformer-engine config you used?

Alex: config I used (abbreviated):
```json
{
  "transformer_engine": {"fp8": true, "recipe": "hybrid", "a_max": null},
  "kernel_policy": ["te_gpt_fp8_fused_attn", "te_gpt_fp16_attn", "fallback_naive"]
}
```
Profiler snippet: 
``
kernel te_gpt_fp8_fused_attn: avg 0.84ms, p95 1.8ms
kernel te_gpt_fp16_attn: avg 1.2ms, p95 2.9ms
fallback naive_attention: avg 3.4ms
tokens/s baseline(fp16): 15900 -> fp8 active: 18000 (median), but tail latency spikes when fallback occurs
```

Jonah: interesting — what's triggering the fallback?

Alex: fallback reasons from logs: 
`WARNING: fp8_calib: scale overflow in layer 5`
`DEBUG: kv_cache: cache_key_len mismatch, invalidating prefix cache for session xyz`
So two things: calibration outliers and KV cache alignment mismatches after prefix reuse.

Priya: do we have per-layer quant stats?

Alex: yes, summary: layers 1-3 stable, layer 5 and 17 show high RMS leading to clamp->fallback. Calibration command used:
```bash
python tools/calibrate_fp8.py --model gpt-medium --data validation1000.jsonl --method layerwise --clip 3.0
```
calib output: "layer 5 scale factor 12.8 (zscore 4.5) -> fallback"

Maya: my hunch: batching heuristic mixing short+long seqs changes activation distributions (KV reuse patterns), causing different dynamic ranges at some layers. Can you try grouping by seq_len instead of naive continuous batching?

Alex: ran grouped-by-length batching. Result: fallback frequency dropped from 9% -> 2%. Throughput became more stable; tail latency reduced ~25%.

Jonah: nice. Another experiment: freeze quant scales in runtime (use offline calib and disable online updates) — should reduce online drift but might slightly degrade rare-token quality.

Alex: ran freeze-scales option: no NaNs, tail latency improved. Quality delta: perplexity +0.6% on our eval set. Fallbacks dropped to <1%.

Priya: good tradeoff. We also saw KV cache invalidations when prefixes reused with different batch alignments — that increases activation variance. We should ensure batching keeps prefix-aligned sessions in the same minibatch.

Maya: proposed action items:
- add kernel selection telemetry tags (fp8_candidate, fallback_reason) to traces
- default batching: group by seq_len for fp8-enabled models
- runtime flag: scale_freeze=true to use offline calibration scales only
- canary rollout: 5% traffic, auto-rollback if fallback_rate > 3% for 10min

Alex: will open PR with the flags + unit/integration tests. Also attaching perf-bot alert rule: fallback_rate > 3% => channel alert.

PerfBot: alert created: perf-alert-4321 targeting #eng-runtime (rule: fp8_fallback_rate > 3% / 10m)

Jonah: one more thought — kernel selection currently prefers fused FP8 kernels but switches to FP16 on overflow. We should consider an intermediate INT8/4-bit path for layers that are brittle. INT8 might be less brittle than FP8 in some cases. Worth an experiment.

Alex: noted. Roadmap: FP8 stabilization first (grouped batching + freeze scales + telemetry). Next, evaluate INT8/4-bit kernels on a small set of layers and microbench.

Maya: can you paste final perf numbers & fallback stats in this thread when PR merges?

Alex: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
